definition_en: costing a lot of money, or causing a high cost
core_image: 商店橱窗里摆着一辆标价很高的山地车，孩子看了价格吐舌头

senses.title: A high price

senses.definitionCN: 价钱很高
senses.example: This bike is too expensive for us.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆自行车对我们来说太贵了。

senses.exampleCN: 这个错误让公司付出了高昂代价。

definition_en: a large hole in the side of a hill or under the ground
core_image: 山坡上开着一个黑暗的洞口，洞口边挂着水珠
scene: 山坡上开着一个黑暗的洞口，洞口边挂着水珠。 They find a cave behind the waterfall.
sceneCN: 这里 cave 是「山洞」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他们在瀑布后面发现一个山洞。

senses.title: A large hole in rock or the ground
senses.definition: a large natural hole in rock or under the ground
senses.definitionCN: 岩体里或地下天然形成的大洞
senses.example: They find a cave behind the waterfall.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在瀑布后面发现一个山洞。
senses.why: Cave came through French from Latin cavus, 'hollow', so the word names a hollow space inside rock.
senses.whyCN: cave 经法语来自拉丁语 cavus「空的」，命名的是岩石里空出来的那块地方。

senses.title: To fall in or collapse
senses.definition: to fall inward or collapse, in the phrase cave in
senses.definitionCN: 向里塌下去，如 cave in
senses.example: The roof caved in under the snow.
senses.why: A hollow can collapse into itself, and English describes that falling in with cave in.
senses.whyCN: 空腔会向自身内部塌下去，英语用 cave in 描述这种塌陷。

senses.title: To give way under pressure
senses.definition: to yield to pressure or demands, in the phrase cave in
senses.definitionCN: 顶不住压力而让步
senses.example: The government caved in to the protests.
senses.exampleCN: 政府在抗议面前让步了。
senses.why: A person who gives way is like a roof caving in: the resistance collapses, so cave in also means to yield.
senses.whyCN: 顶不住的人就像塌下去的屋顶，抵抗力垮了，所以 cave in 也表示屈服。

definition_en: a feathered animal that can usually fly, or informally a person
core_image: 一只小东西落在枝头，羽毛蓬起，喉咙发出短促的鸣叫
scene: 清晨窗外，一只小东西在枝头跳了两下，叫了一声。 A bird sang outside my window.
sceneCN: 这里 bird 是「鸟」（第 01 个义项）；句意是一只鸟在我窗外鸣叫。

derivatives.zh: 由 bird 加 -ie 构成，义为「小鸟」

senses.title: A feathered animal with wings
senses.definition: a warm-blooded animal with feathers and wings, usually able to fly
senses.definitionCN: 有羽毛和翅膀、通常会飞的温血动物
senses.example: A bird sang outside my window.
senses.why: Bird comes from Old English bridd, first used of young nestlings and later of the whole feathered kind.
senses.whyCN: bird 来自古英语 bridd，最初指巢里的雏鸟，后来扩大到所有有羽毛的鸟类。

senses.title: An odd or unusual person, in informal talk
senses.definition: a person, especially an odd or unusual one, in informal speech
senses.definitionCN: 口语里指人，尤指古怪特别的人
senses.example: He is a funny old bird.
senses.why: Calling a person a bird borrows the creature's odd habits and quick movements, so the word can label a peculiar character.
senses.whyCN: 把人叫作 bird，是借鸟的古怪习性和灵活动作来打比方，于是这个词能指性格特别的人。

senses.title: Someone who acts early, in early bird
senses.definition: a person who arrives or acts early, in the phrase early bird
senses.definitionCN: 在 early bird 中指起得早、到得早的人
senses.example: The early birds got the best seats.
senses.exampleCN: 早到的人坐到了最好的位置。
senses.why: Birds sing before sunrise, so an early bird became the picture of anyone who is first on the scene.
senses.whyCN: 鸟在日出前就鸣叫，于是 early bird 成了「最早到场的人」的画面。

definition_en: a unit of measurement, an amount, or an academic rank
core_image: 墙上的温度计指针停在三十度，窗外是烈日
scene: 墙上的温度计指针停在三十度，窗外是烈日。 The thermometer shows thirty degrees.
sceneCN: 这里 degree 是「度」（第 01 个义项）；句意是温度计显示三十度。

senses.title: A unit for measuring temperature or angles
senses.definition: a unit marked on a scale for measuring temperature or angles
senses.definitionCN: 温度计或角度刻度上的计量单位
senses.example: The thermometer shows thirty degrees.
senses.why: Latin de- plus gradus, a step, gave degree, one step on a scale; a thermometer is such a scale, so each mark is a degree.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 de- 加 gradus「台阶」构成 degree，即刻度上的一格；温度计正是这样一把刻度尺，每一格就是一度。

senses.title: The amount or level of something
senses.definition: the amount, level or extent to which something is true
senses.definitionCN: 某事成立的程度或深浅
senses.example: The two stories differ in degree, not in kind.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个说法差别在程度上，不在性质上。
senses.why: A step on a scale also measures how far something has gone, so degree came to mean the extent of a quality rather than a fixed unit.
senses.whyCN: 刻度上的一格也量出某事物走到了多远，于是 degree 从固定单位引申为某种性质的程度。

senses.title: An academic rank from a university
senses.definition: a rank given by a university to someone who has completed a course of study
senses.definitionCN: 大学授予完成学业者的学术等级
senses.example: She has a degree in history.
senses.why: University study was once organised as a series of graded steps, and the rank reached at the end kept the name degree.
senses.whyCN: 大学学业曾按一级一级的台阶组织，走到终点所获的等级就沿用了 degree 这个名字。

definition_en: in fact or truly, or used to strengthen a statement, or to show surprise
core_image: 孩子把自己的画举到老师面前，认真地指着画里的小人
scene: 孩子把自己的画举到老师面前，认真地指着画里的小人。 I really like this book.
sceneCN: 这里 really 是「真正地」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我真的很喜欢这本书。

senses.title: In fact, truly
senses.definition: In fact, truly
senses.definitionCN: 确实如此，不是假象
senses.example: I really like this book.
senses.why: Really is real plus the adverb ending ly, so it says a thing is so in fact and not only in appearance.
senses.whyCN: really 是 real 加副词词尾 ly，表示事情确实如此，不只是表面。

senses.title: Used to strengthen what follows

senses.why: In everyday speech the word of truth turned into a plain intensifier: what is really good is simply very good.
senses.whyCN: 日常口语中，表示“确实”的词变成单纯的加强语：really good 就是非常好。

senses.title: Used to show surprise or doubt

definition_en: feeling pleasure, pleased, or willing to do something
core_image: 一个孩子抱着刚拿到的风筝，在草地上笑着跑
scene: 草地上，一个孩子抱着新风筝笑着奔跑。 The children were happy with the new kite.
sceneCN: 这里 happy 是「快乐的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是孩子们对新风筝很满意。

pos.zh: 形容词：快乐的、满意的、乐意的

senses.title: Feeling pleasure and joy
senses.definition: feeling pleasure or joy
senses.definitionCN: 心里感到愉快、喜悦
senses.example: The children were happy with the new kite.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们很喜欢新风筝，很开心。
senses.why: Happy comes from happ, 'chance, good luck'; to be happy was first to have good fortune, then to feel the pleasure it brings.
senses.whyCN: happy 来自 happ「机缘、好运」，最初指碰上了好运气，后来指好运气带来的愉快心情。

senses.title: Pleased with a result
senses.definition: satisfied with something that has happened
senses.definitionCN: 对已经发生的事感到称心
senses.example: She was happy with the result.
senses.why: A good outcome is good fortune, so being happy with something means finding it satisfactory.
senses.whyCN: 好结果就是好运，所以 happy with 某事物就是觉得它称心如意。

senses.title: Willing to do something
senses.definition: willing and glad to do something
senses.definitionCN: 心甘情愿、乐于去做
senses.example: I am happy to help.
senses.why: A person who feels no reluctance about a task is pleased at the chance to do it, hence happy to do.
senses.whyCN: 对一件事毫不勉强，就是为有机会做它而高兴，于是有 happy to do 的说法。

items.en: The word now covers pleasure, satisfaction and willingness.
items.cn: 现代英语中它涵盖快乐、满意与乐意。

items.cn: 它还出现在祝福语与气氛描写中。

definition_en: the seventh month of the year, between June and August
core_image: 盛夏午后，阳光把泳池照得发亮
scene: 七月我们放暑假，常去游泳。 In July we are on summer holiday and often go swimming.
sceneCN: 这里 July 是「七月」（第 1 个义项：一年中的第七个月，在六月与八月之间）；句意：七月我们放暑假，常去游泳。

senses.title: The seventh month of the year
senses.definition: the seventh month of the calendar year, with thirty-one days
senses.definitionCN: 公历年的第七个月，有三十一天
senses.example: July is the hottest month here.
senses.exampleCN: 七月是这里最热的月份。
senses.why: The month is named for Julius Caesar and falls in the heat of summer.
senses.whyCN: 这个月以尤利乌斯·凯撒命名，正处在盛夏的炎热中。

senses.title: Midsummer and the summer holiday
senses.definition: the month felt as the height of summer and the heart of the long holiday
senses.definitionCN: 被感受为盛夏顶点和漫长假期的核心的那个月
senses.example: Swimming pools are busy in July.
senses.why: Heat and free time combine, so the month becomes a symbol of summer leisure.
senses.whyCN: 炎热与空闲时间结合，这个月成为夏日休闲的象征。

senses.title: The month in history and holidays
senses.definition: the month used for national holidays and historical dates
senses.definitionCN: 用于国庆节和历史日期的月份
senses.example: Many national holidays fall in July.
senses.why: Warm weather and long days make the month a common choice for national celebrations.
senses.whyCN: 温暖的天气和长日使这个月成为国庆庆祝的常见选择。

intro.en: July is the month of Julius Caesar, renamed in his honour over two thousand years ago.

items.en: The month is renamed Iulius after Julius Caesar.
items.cn: 这个月以尤利乌斯·凯撒之名改称 Iulius。

items.en: The name passes into French as juillet.
items.cn: 这个名字以 juillet 进入法语。

items.en: English borrows it as Julie or July.
items.cn: 英语借入时写作 Julie 或 July。

items.en: The spelling settles as July.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 July。

definition_en: a game in which players throw a ball through a high hoop, or the ball used
core_image: 一只橙色的球被抛向高处的圆环，网绳轻轻一颤
scene: 操场的篮架下，几个孩子把球传来传去，等着出手。 They played basketball until the light faded.
sceneCN: 这里 basketball 是「篮球运动」（第 01 个义项）；句意是他们打篮球打到天光暗下去。

由 basketball 与 court 复合，义为「篮球场」

senses.title: The game played with a ball and a high basket
senses.definition: a game in which two teams try to throw a ball through a high net
senses.definitionCN: 两队把球投进高处的篮网的运动
senses.example: They played basketball until the light faded.
senses.exampleCN: 他们打篮球一直打到天光暗下去。
senses.why: The name joins basket and ball, and the game is named after its two fixed pieces: the ball and the basket it must reach.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字由 basket 和 ball 合成，这项运动正是以它固定的两样东西命名：球，以及球要投进的篮筐。

senses.title: The ball used in that game
senses.definition: the large round ball used in the game of basketball
senses.definitionCN: 篮球运动中使用的大圆球
senses.example: He bounced the basketball twice before shooting.
senses.exampleCN: 他投篮前把篮球拍了两下。
senses.why: Taken word by word, basketball is simply 'basket ball', the ball aimed at the basket, and that literal object is still the second sense.
senses.whyCN: 逐字看，basketball 就是「篮子球」，即投向篮筐的那颗球；这个字面所指的实物仍是它的第二个义项。

definition_en: a bicycle, or a series of events that repeat
core_image: 一辆自行车靠在树旁，车轮的影子在地上画出一个圆
scene: 一辆自行车靠在树旁，车轮的影子在地上画出一个圆。 He cycles to school every morning.
sceneCN: 这里 cycle 是「骑自行车」（第 03 个义项）；句意是他每天早上骑车上学。

senses.title: A bicycle
senses.definition: a bicycle, used especially in written or formal British English
senses.definitionCN: 自行车，多见于英国书面或正式说法
senses.example: He cycles to school every morning.
senses.why: Greek kyklos, a circle, gave English cycle; the two-wheeled machine was named for its wheels going round, and the short noun kept that name.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 kyklos「圆」演变出 cycle；两个轮子转圈的车因此得名，名词形式保留了这个称呼。

senses.title: A series of events that repeats
senses.definition: a set of events that happen again and again in the same order
senses.definitionCN: 按同样顺序反复出现的一串事情
senses.example: The seasons follow a yearly cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 四季按一年的周期循环。
senses.why: The original sense of kyklos was a circle, and a circle returns to where it started, so any repeating round of events is a cycle.
senses.whyCN: kyklos 本义是圆圈，圆圈走一圈又回到起点，所以任何反复一轮的事情都叫 cycle。

senses.title: To ride a bicycle
senses.definition: to travel by bicycle
senses.definitionCN: 骑自行车出行
senses.example: She cycles to the park on Sundays.
senses.why: The verb simply turns the bicycle noun into the action of using it, the way many vehicle names become verbs.
senses.whyCN: 动词只是把「自行车」这个名词变成使用它的动作，很多交通工具名称都这样转化为动词。

definition_en: covered with dirt, or to make something dirty
core_image: 一双沾满泥的球鞋放在门口，旁边是干净的地板
scene: 一双沾满泥的球鞋放在门口，旁边是干净的地板。 His shoes are dirty after the rain.
sceneCN: 这里 dirty 是「脏的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是雨后他的鞋很脏。

senses.title: Covered with dirt
senses.definition: covered or marked with dirt, dust or stains
senses.definitionCN: 沾上泥土、灰尘或污渍
senses.example: His shoes are dirty after the rain.
senses.why: Dirt came from Old Norse drit, filth, and the adjective simply says that something is covered with it.
senses.whyCN: dirt 来自古北欧语 drit「污物」，形容词直接表示某物沾满了这种东西。

senses.title: To make something dirty
senses.definition: to get dirt or stains onto something
senses.definitionCN: 把泥土或污渍弄到某物上
senses.example: The mud dirtied her white dress.
senses.exampleCN: 泥巴弄脏了她的白裙子。
senses.why: The adjective turned into a verb: making something dirty is putting dirt where it was clean.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成动词：让东西变脏，就是把污物带到原本干净的地方。

senses.title: Unfair or dishonest
senses.definition: unfair, dishonest or cruel, used about actions and tricks
senses.definitionCN: 形容手段不公平、不诚实或阴损
senses.example: It was a dirty trick to hide her shoes.
senses.exampleCN: 把她的鞋藏起来是个卑劣的把戏。
senses.why: Filth was long used as an image for moral foulness, so a dirty trick is a trick that leaves the same stain on the people who play it.
senses.whyCN: 污秽历来被用来比喻道德上的败坏，所以 dirty trick 就是会让使坏者自己也沾上污点的把戏。
